facts.name: Golden Ragwort
facts.light: Part shade to shade; full sun only with steady moisture
facts.notes: A spreading groundcover of rounded, heart-shaped leaves that stay green most of the year, topped in late spring by clusters of bright yellow daisies on 1 to 2 ft stems. Good for wet, shady spots and rain gardens. It spreads by roots and seed and can get a little weedy.
facts.toxSrc: NC State Extension lists low-severity poison in the leaves

sources.title: MSU Native Plants: Golden ragwort fact sheet
sources.note: MSU prairie fen fact sheet (as Senecio aureus): Michigan native; blooms May to June; 6 in to 2.5 ft tall.

sources.title: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox: Golden Ragwort
sources.note: Low-severity poison. Spent flowers look untidy, so cut them back to the leafy base, or leave the seeds for birds. Self-seeds and can colonize.

companions.why: Companions: blue flag iris, cinnamon fern, marsh marigold, foam flower, wild columbine and wild blue phlox.
